title: Regular pullback of the logarithmic dualizing line along a nodal modification
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be projective flat finitely presented morphisms with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional geometric fibres having only ordinary double points. Give $X$ and $Y$ pairwise disjoint sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ in their relative smooth loci. Use the marked-family and canonical relative-dualizing-module conventions of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction], without positivity; put $D_X=\sum_j a_j(S)$, $D_Y=\sum_j b_j(S)$ and $L_X=\omega_{X/R}(D_X)$, $L_Y=\omega_{Y/R}(D_Y)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let $p:Y\to X$ be a proper $S$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $p b_j=a_j$, for which some finite set $Z$ of closed points of the special fibre of $X$ has $p^{-1}(X\setminus Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}X\setminus Z$. Then the canonical isomorphism $p^*L_X\cong L_Y$ on $p^{-1}(X\setminus Z)$ extends to an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear morphism $\alpha_p:p^*L_X\to L_Y$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its restriction to the generic fibre is the usual pullback isomorphism of logarithmic dualizing line bundles for $p_K$. This assertion concerns the line bundles and their morphism, not their modules of global sections. Neither stability nor smooth generic fibre nor normal total space is assumed, and $n=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent logarithmic discrepancy formulation motivated by Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), using the adjunction normalization in def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum. Tag 0CDC computes the blowup charts, not this theorem. A precise reference including horizontal persistent nodes and markings is WANTED: Knudsen, The projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves II, sections 1--2.

proof.text: Put $U=p^{-1}(X\setminus Z)$ and $M=(p^*L_X)^\vee\otimes L_Y$. The canonical invertible dualizing lines and their Cartier marking twists give this invertible Hom module. The given marked-family isomorphism on $U$ supplies $s_U\in\Gamma(U,M)$. Since $Z$ lies in the special fibre, $Y_K\subset U$ and its restriction $s_K$ is the canonical pullback for the isomorphism $p_K$.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog), reduction to an invertible Hom module; agent setup

proof.text: For a special-fibre component generic point $\eta$ whose image in $X$ is relatively smooth, apply the smooth-image integrality lemma. Its hypotheses hold for the same marked families and $p_K$; properness of $p$ is unnecessary for it. Thus $s_K\in M_\eta$. This includes images on a marked section and uses no assumption that the generic fibre is wholly smooth.

source.place: Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), centred smooth-section coordinates; agent logarithmic-integrality argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 2, 4 and 5, using algebra.tex lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module and duality.tex lemma-fundamental-class-lci. Not a verbatim assertion of the tag.

proof.text: If $p(\eta)$ is nonsmooth, apply the nodal-image integrality lemma to the same data and the original canonical generic comparison. It gives $s_K\in M_\eta$, including persistent nodes. Together with the preceding case this verifies integrality at every special-fibre component generic point.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family); agent branch-integrality and faithfully flat pole-quotient argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 2, 3, 6 and 7. Normalization uses duality.tex lemma-fundamental-class-lci and lemma-shriek-etale. Not a verbatim assertion of the tag.

proof.text: Apply the trait line-section extension lemma to $(Y,M,U,s_U)$. The morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat and of finite type, its special fibre is reduced and pure one-dimensional, and the preceding two steps supply all required integral germs. We obtain a section $s\in\Gamma(Y,M)$ restricting to $s_U$.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog), combined with algebra.tex lemma-criterion-reduced and lemma-apply-grothendieck; agent generic-germ spreading and depth argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 1 and 8--10. The tag alone assumes the depth condition, whereas this statement derives it from the reduced curve special fibre.

proof.text: Evaluate $s$ as a homomorphism of the two invertible modules: on a local frame $e$ of $p^*L_X$, write $s=e^\vee\otimes v$ and set $\alpha_p(e)=v$; changes of frame give the same map. Since $s|_U=s_U$, this map is the prescribed isomorphism on $U$ and therefore the usual pullback on $Y_K$. For $n=0$ the marked case is absent. No stability, positivity or normality has entered.
